elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Company may also terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience, for any or no reason..." — Statement of Work is this MSA's Order Form analogue (defined in §1(a)), so both the master agreement and individual engagements are covered.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "...upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor" — exactly 30 days, in writing, no additional conditions or consent triggers.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "...in which case Contractor shall refund any prepaid fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of such termination." The word "pro rata" is express, not inferred from the post-termination period alone.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "Contractor may not terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience while any Statement of Work is outstanding." The only retained Contractor convenience right (§6(a), 15 days) is by its own terms available only "[a]t any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding," so the two provisions do not overlap; the sole period of commitment under this indefinite MSA is while an SOW is open, and Contractor is barred throughout it. §6(b) is for-cause only and is not a convenience right.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right runs on thirty (30) days' notice, which is below the 60–90 day fallback band (and better for Customer); no 60–90 day mechanic appears anywhere.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: neither §6 nor the insertion imposes any early-termination fee, penalty, or acceleration on Company; §6(b) only requires payment of fees "incurred or earned ... through the effective date of such termination." With no fee to cap, the element is satisfied vacuously.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Retained §6(a) lets Contractor terminate "for any or no reason" whenever no SOW is outstanding; that is a gap-period right, not a right whose effective date is tied to the end of a then-current term (this MSA has no fixed term to anchor to).

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Retained §6(a) requires only "fifteen (15) days advance notice" from Contractor; the insertion bars but does not re-time that right.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met in operative language (30-day Company convenience right over the Agreement or any Statement of Work, express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Contractor convenience termination while any SOW is outstanding).

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a substance-check artefact, not a defect: it evidently keys on the pre-redline text (or on the alias "Customer" rather than the document's defined "Company"). The rendered operative sentence expressly grants Company a convenience termination right, so the coverage and minimality gates that passed reflect the true state.

Minimality holds: nothing in §2, §6(a) or §6(b) is deleted or paraphrased, the Customer-favourable mutual 15-day gap-period right survives verbatim, and the insertion adds only what elements 1–4 require. The "in whole or in part" surplus from the model language was correctly omitted, and no survival tail, expense allocation, or extra procedure was bolted on. The phrase "for any or no reason" mirrors retained §6(a) drafting and does not add an operative requirement.

Intent preserved: the Contractor bar and retained §6(a) occupy mutually exclusive periods (SOW outstanding vs. none outstanding), so no retained sentence is contradicted; §6(b)'s for-cause mechanics, the payment-through-termination sentence, the Works-in-progress assignment, and the §2 cross-reference to Paragraph 6 all remain intact with no dangling term.

Fallback is not independently satisfied (30-day notice sits outside the 60–90 band and Contractor's notice/timing is untouched), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is complete; no repair is required.
